RSTP, L2_unicast, power_cycle

[Log-derived analysis] Layer-2 redundancy under RSTP. Builds a multi-member stack plus partner switches with RSTP running for loop prevention, runs a steady L2 unicast traffic stream and confirms baseline connectivity over a loop-free topology. It then hardware power-cycles the stack Active Master to force an unplanned failover and analyses captured-packet gaps for disruption. Confirms spanning-tree keeps the L2 topology loop-free and re-converges across the failover. Verifies the backup member takes over as stack Active Master, the rebooted unit cleanly rejoins and resyncs the stack, stack ports return to their expected state, channel-group/LAG diagnostics stay clean, per-failover traffic disruption stays within acceptable thresholds, the running-config is preserved after teardown, and no exceptions or core dumps occur.

diff -B option ignores more than just blank lines

The egress-rate-limit can not apply the configuration correctly on VCS.

An unnecessary log is outputted, when IPv6 Multicast Packet is received.

The forwarded packet by UDP broadcast helper could be wrong

If IGMP Snooping feature is disabled. multicast packets does not flood after V2 or V3 report packets was received.

Regardless of ACL deny action is set, packet which is matched the ACL isnt disarded occasionally.

Stack: The log size config was removed after rolling reboot.

MAC Thrashing Traps are sent out when thrash-limiting action none.

Private-vlans: Kernel Panic on de-configuring private-vlans

Port not working in new VLAN after private-vlan configuration is removed from it

Broadcom switches send back NLB heartbeat packet to receiving port, resulting in ping fail to actual IP address

LAG configuration with private-vlan is removed after VCS failover

NSM core dump while deconfiguring channel-group

NSM core dumps on x930 and DC2552XS following adding/removing IGMP proxy configuration

GS948MX 'show platform port' causes 10G SFP+ port link down / UP

Show system broken after change the stack management subnet

description:
If the reason for the failure to deliver is that the route to the destination is a reject route, the Code field is set to 6. This may occur if the router has been configured to reject all the traffic for a specific prefix. AND Site border routers SHOULD install a black hole route for the Local IPv6 prefix FC00::/7. This will insure that packets with Local IPv6 destination addresses will not be forwarded outside of the site via a default route. Site border routers SHOULD respond with the appropriate ICMPv6 Destination Unreachable message to inform the source that the packet was not forwarded [ICMPV6]. This feedback is important to avoid transport protocol timeouts. (Note: Second paragraph of section 6.0 in draft talks about a black hole route for Local IPv6 prefix FC00::/7 and an appropriate ICMPv6 destination unreachable message.
